key_terms.meaning: the <?php … ?> region of a .php file; everything outside it is sent to the browser as plain HTML
a name starting with $ that holds a value fixed at run time; no type declaration is written
the single value that means 'no value'; a variable is NULL before anything is assigned to it
PHP converts between int, float, string and bool by itself when an operator needs it
a free installer that puts Apache, PHP and MySQL on one laptop for local testing
the part of a Java web server that loads a servlet, calls its methods and writes the response; Tomcat is one
a PHP array whose keys are names, not positions, e.g. $marks['maths'] = 90
loop that visits every key and value of an array without a counter
a variable born inside a function dies when the function returns unless it is declared global
a pattern such as /^[0-9]{10}$/ used to test or rewrite text
PCRE function that returns 1 when the pattern is found in the string, 0 when it is not
superglobal array holding the fields sent in the URL query string
superglobal array holding the fields sent in the request body
a form whose action is the same page, so one script draws the form and later processes it
PHP function that asks the browser to keep a name=value pair and send it back later
creates or resumes a server-side session and gives the browser a cookie holding only the session ID
init once, service on every request, destroy once — all called by the container
a Java object that JSF creates and links to page fields by name
Spring annotation marking a class whose method return values become the response body, usually JSON
an interface you declare; Spring Data writes the SQL behind findAll(), save() and friends

takeaways: A .php file is HTML with PHP islands; the server runs the islands and sends only the result.
PHP variables are $names with no declared type, so the same name can hold an int and later a string.
XAMPP is for learning on a laptop: Apache serves, PHP interprets, MySQL stores.
Control statements and functions are the same ideas as in C or Java, but PHP arrays are ordered maps that foreach walks directly.
Regular expressions move validation from long if-chains to one pattern string.
GET puts form data in the URL, POST puts it in the body; a self-submitting page reads one or the other.
Cookies live in the browser and are small; sessions live on the server and the browser keeps only the ID.
A servlet is one object reused for many requests: the container calls init once, service per request, destroy once.
JSP and JSF are built on top of the servlet API, not beside it.
Spring Boot removes the external server step: the server is inside the JAR, and a controller method becomes a JSON endpoint.
bank_note: Long answers usually ask you to explain a mechanism and then write or read short code — life cycle order, GET versus POST, cookie versus session, and one working PHP or servlet example.

bank.q: Explain step by step what happens when a browser requests a .php page, and describe PHP's scalar data types with one example of each.
outline: Browser asks Apache for the file by URL
Server sees the .php extension and passes it to the PHP interpreter, not the browser
Interpreter runs only the <?php ?> blocks, leaves HTML alone
Output stream is returned to Apache, then to the browser as plain HTML
int, float, string, bool each with a one-line example; NULL means no value
No type declaration; type juggling converts on demand

bank.q: Distinguish a web server, a PHP interpreter and a servlet container. Where does a package like XAMPP fit in?
outline: Web server: speaks HTTP, gives files and hands dynamic requests on
PHP interpreter: executes PHP blocks and returns output
Servlet container: loads Java servlet classes, calls init/service/destroy
Tomcat and IIS can both act as containers; Apache plus PHP module handles PHP
XAMPP bundles Apache, PHP, MySQL and Perl for one laptop
Ports and document root explained briefly

bank.q: Describe the servlet life cycle. State which method runs how many times and who calls it.
outline: Container loads the class and creates one instance
init() once, after construction, for setup
service() for every request; it dispatches to doGet or doPost
destroy() once before the object is removed
Programmer overrides methods, never calls them
One instance may serve many requests on different threads, so instance fields are shared

bank.q: Compare the GET and POST methods: where the data travels, size limits, visibility and what PHP gives you to read it.
outline: GET appends name=value pairs to the URL after ?
POST sends them in the request body
GET is visible in history and logs, POST is not
GET has practical URL length limits, POST is meant for larger data
PHP: $_GET, $_POST, and $_REQUEST for both
Neither is secure by itself — HTTPS is what protects the data

bank.q: Write a self-submitting PHP page that takes a student's name and marks and prints the grade using if / else if.
outline: Form with method="post" and action set to the same file, or no action
Check $_SERVER['REQUEST_METHOD'] or isset($_POST['submit'])
Read fields, cast marks to int
if / else if chain for grade bands
Print with echo, escape output
Show the form again when not submitted

bank.q: Write PHP code using regular expressions to validate a 10-digit mobile number and an email address, and to mask the first six digits of the number.
outline: preg_match with /^[6-9][0-9]{9}$/ for the number
filter_var or a pattern for the email
preg_replace with a pattern to replace leading digits by *
Return values explained: 1 found, 0 not found, false on error
Say that validation must be repeated on the server

bank.q: Write a login page that stores the user name in a session, greets the user on later pages and provides logout.
outline: session_start() at the top of every page
Check password, then set $_SESSION['user']
Guard pages with isset($_SESSION['user'])
Logout: session_unset() and session_destroy()
Contrast with a cookie that would expose the name to the browser
Mention session ID cookie and expiry

bank.q: Write a servlet that reads two numbers from an HTML form and prints their sum, showing doGet and the response content type.
outline: Class extends HttpServlet
doGet(HttpServletRequest, HttpServletResponse)
setContentType("text/html") before writing
request.getParameter for both fields, parse with Integer.parseInt
PrintWriter out = response.getWriter()
Handle NumberFormatException with a message

bank.q: Build a PHP associative array of five students and their marks, sort it by marks, and print it using foreach.
outline: Array literal with named keys, or keys added one by one
arsort() keeps keys while sorting by value
foreach ($arr as $name => $mark) syntax
echo with formatting inside the loop
Count with count()
Mention that PHP arrays are ordered maps

bank.q: Write a Spring Boot REST controller with one endpoint that saves an entity and one that lists all rows, using a JPA repository.
outline: @RestController and @RequestMapping paths
Repository interface extends JpaRepository<Entity, Long>
@GetMapping returns List, Spring serialises to JSON
@PostMapping with @RequestBody binds the JSON to the entity
save() and findAll() explained
Embedded Tomcat started by main()

bank.q: HTTP is called stateless. Discuss this, then compare cookies and sessions on storage place, size, security and lifetime.
outline: Each request is independent; server keeps no memory of the last one
Statelessness helps scaling but breaks login and carts
Cookie: small value stored in the browser, sent on every request, editable by the user
Session: data on the server, browser keeps only the ID
Cookie size limit of about 4 KB per cookie
Session ID must travel over HTTPS; expiry and session fixation

bank.q: Compare PHP with Java servlets and JSP as server-side technologies: compilation, threading, database access and hosting cost.
outline: PHP: interpreted per request, quick to deploy, cheap shared hosting
Servlets: compiled bytecode, JVM, one instance on many threads
JSP compiles to a servlet on first use
Both talk to databases through a driver; PHP uses PDO or mysqli, Java uses JDBC or JPA
Java gives strong typing and a large library; PHP gives a shorter learning curve
Choose by team skills, expected load, hosting budget

bank.q: A form accepts a phone number and a date. Evaluate client-side and server-side validation, and show how a PHP regular expression fits the server side.
outline: Client-side checks give fast feedback but can be bypassed or switched off
Server-side check is the only one that protects the data
preg_match pattern for the phone number, date checked against a format
Always re-check and escape before storing or printing
Cost of rejecting bad data at the database layer
Both layers together; never trust $_POST

bank.q: Explain how a JSP page becomes a servlet, how JSF adds components and beans, and how Spring Boot changes the deployment step.
outline: JSP translated to Java source, then compiled to a servlet class
Life cycle is the servlet life cycle; jspService handles the request
JSF: reusable UI components, a component tree, managed beans bound by name, navigation rules
Spring Boot: starter dependencies, auto-configuration, embedded Tomcat
Build produces an executable JAR or a WAR for an external container
@RestController method returning an object becomes a JSON body

glossary.def: Code that runs on the web server and sends only its output to the browser, so the source is never seen by the user.
A scripting language designed for web pages, embedded inside HTML inside <?php ?> tags.
A program that reads code and executes it line by line instead of compiling it to a file first.
The folder a web server treats as the top of the website, so a file there is reached by its path in the URL.
A PHP array such as $_GET, $_POST, $_COOKIE or $_SESSION that is available in every scope without a global keyword.
A name defined once with define() or const whose value cannot change afterwards.
The fixed order in which operators in one expression are evaluated, e.g. * before +.
A function that calls itself on a smaller input, with a base case that stops the calls.
A PHP array whose keys are 0, 1, 2 … by default, like a list.
Perl Compatible Regular Expressions, the pattern flavour used by PHP's preg_* family.
The part of a URL after ?, holding name=value pairs joined by &.
The part of an HTTP request after the headers that carries form data or other content.
A small name=value string the server asks the browser to store and return on later requests to that site.
Server-side storage tied to one visitor by a session ID, used for logins and carts.
A long random string that links a browser's cookie to the right server-side session data.
A Java class extending HttpServlet that the container calls to answer HTTP requests.
The web.xml file that maps servlet classes to URL patterns and sets startup and session options.
JavaServer Pages: an HTML file with Java pieces that the container translates into a servlet.
A Java object whose life cycle JSF controls and whose properties page fields read and write.
JavaServer Faces: a component-based Java web framework built on servlets.
A Spring framework layer that auto-configures an application and starts an embedded server.
A container creates an object's collaborators and passes them in, instead of the object creating them.
Object-relational mapping: linking Java class fields to database table columns so you work in objects, not SQL strings.
Jakarta Persistence API, the standard set of annotations and interfaces used for ORM in Java.
A URL whose response is JSON data rather than an HTML page, usually consumed by a front end or app.
